item.description: El 28 de febrero de 2026, Estados Unidos e Israel lanzaron ataques conjuntos contra Irán en un conflicto que se prometía de semanas y que ahora cumple seis años. Con numerosas muertes, un estancamiento en las negociaciones y el cierre del estrecho de Ormuz, la guerra ha desatado una crisis en el sector energético global e incertidumbre en los mercados. ¿Cuál es la posición diplomática de Washington y su capacidad defensiva? ¿Cómo se lee el cambio de postura de Donald Trump? item.title: Show HN: Sesame - a local-first, open-source password manager
item.description: I have been working on Sesame, an open-source password manager that keeps your vault local by default. You don't need an account to create or use a vault, and the hosted service never receives the vault itself. It's still early software and the independent security review isn't finished yet, so I am mainly interested in feedback, testing, and people looking through the code. (Linux support is yet to be released on v0.1.2, but currently is in the works.) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49483038 Points: 39 # Comments: 42 Fuente: Hacker News - Portada.

item.title: Can Trump really rename Lake Ontario, ‘Lake America’?
item.description: Mark Carney rejects attempt to rename lake as did several US governors, with Tony Evers mocking the move US politics live – latest updates Donald Trump signed an executive order on Thursday directing the federal government to rename Lake Ontario, making it Lake America, amid his escalating trade war with Canada. The order directs federal agencies to adopt the name-change on US maps, documents and databases. But Trump has no authority to rename Canada’s portion of the lake, nor to compel Canada, international legal bodies, international mapmakers or the rest of the world to adopt a new name… Publicado también por: BBC News - World, The Guardian - World, The Jerusalem Post - International. item.title: Japan's controversial WWII heroes: How one kamikaze pilot escaped certain death
item.description: Towards the end of World War II, as US troops advanced across the Pacific, Japan resorted to a desperate strategy: kamikaze attacks. Thousands of Japanese pilots, with an average age of just 21, were ordered to crash their explosive-laden planes into enemy ships. More than 3,800 pilots gave up their lives, killing over 7,000 allied naval personnel. Our reporter Mélodie Sforza met one of the last surviving former kamikaze pilots. Fuente: France 24 - English.
